name: low-baseline-prompt-intervention-20260825
description: Prompt and scaffold interventions on tasks where the model under test is measurably weak. Derived from the only supported result the system has produced: on BIG-Bench object_counting an explicit counting algorithm with three demonstrations took numeric_accuracy from 0.32 to 0.63 (paired permutation p=0.000999). The 26 completed runs of the scaffold agenda that found at most +1.5 points all sat on baselines between 0.67 and 0.82, so headroom -- not intervention cleverness -- is what separated them. Candidates must therefore target a task whose measured baseline leaves room to move, and must be executable by a registered runner: the intervention is the prompt or the input text, never the weights, the architecture or the inference engine.

prefer.baseline_headroom_rule: report the unmodified-input baseline first; a task whose baseline exceeds 0.6 needs an explicit argument for why headroom remains

reject.reason: V1 registers two runners, generative_qa and sequence_classification, whose candidate hook is the prompt or the input text; anything else cannot be executed and is refused at preflight

required_output.terminal_rule: first supported => T1; ten scientifically decided without supported => T2
measurement_requirements: report the unmodified-input baseline and the candidate under an equal generation budget
a paired significance test with its permutation count
raw predictions retained so an arm that generated nothing cannot pass as a refutation
